issues.detail: The Greek 'εγκρατευεται' (enkrateuetai) means 'exercises self-control' or 'is self-controlled.' The Vietnamese 'kiêng kỵ mọi sự' translates to 'abstains from all things' or 'refrains from everything,' which is a different concept than the internal discipline of self-control.

The Greek 'φθαρτον στεφανον' means 'perishable crown.' The Vietnamese 'mão triều thiên hay hư nát' is confusingly phrased; it seems to conflate the 'perishable crown' with a choice ('hay' meaning 'or'), whereas the Greek describes the nature of the crown they are receiving.
